No. The federal EIA table does not list Roulet 12 and 13 yet, so keep both units as construction and look again in the next EIA monthly table due November 24, 2026.

Where to find it:
- EIA: open the EIA-860M workbook for September 2026 at https://www.eia.gov/electricity/data/eia860m/xls/september_generator2026.xlsx. On the sheet named Planned there is no row with Plant Name Anadarko Plant or Plant ID 3006. On the Operating sheet the Anadarko Plant rows 4375 to 4382 are older units, none of them the new turbines.
- Oklahoma permit memorandum dated October 29, 2024, at https://applications.deq.ok.gov/permitspublic/storedpermits/8827.pdf. Page 3 of the PDF says the project adds two LM6000PC-SPRINT simple cycle combustion turbines. Page 9 of the PDF, in the table headed LM6000 PC SPRINT Simple Cycle - Operating Assumptions (per unit), has the row Gross Generation 50,182 kW per CT.
- Southwest Power Pool queue list at https://opsportal.spp.org/Studies/GenerateActiveCSV, saved on November 5, 2026 and showing Last Updated On 11/3/2026. records.question: Which EIA generator ids belong to Comanche CC2 and CC3?
records.finding: The EIA-860M table for September 2026 at https://www.eia.gov/electricity/data/eia860m/xls/september_generator2026.xlsx lists generators 2G1 at 408.8 MW and 2S1 at 277.6 MW with unit code CC2. records.recommendation: Treat 2G1 and 2S1 as CC2, and 3G1 and 3S1 as CC3. Type these ids into Other IDs for the unit by hand in the web form.
records.researcher_notes:
This card asks which Energy Information Administration (EIA) generator ids belong to Comanche CC2 and CC3. EIA's own unit code column names the blocks, so there is no doubt about the pairing.

Where to find it:
- Source: the EIA-860M table for September 2026 at https://www.eia.gov/electricity/data/eia860m/xls/september_generator2026.xlsx.
- Open the sheet named "Planned". Find Plant ID 8059, Plant Name "Comanche (OK)". Read the columns "Generator ID", "Unit Code" and "Nameplate Capacity (MW)".
- Generator 2G1 shows Unit Code CC2 and 408.8 MW. Generator 2S1 shows Unit Code CC2 and 277.6 MW.
- Generator 3G1 shows Unit Code CC3 and 408.8 MW. Generator 3S1 shows Unit Code CC3 and 277.6 MW.
- The column "Technology" reads "Natural Gas Fired Combined Cycle" on all four rows. Each pair is a gas turbine plus a steam turbine, so each pair is one combined cycle block.

Why the EIA status is out of date:
- The columns "Planned Operation Month" and "Planned Operation Year" read 9 and 2029 on all four rows, which is September 2029.
- The column "Status" reads "(P) Planned for installation, but regulatory approvals not initiated". That is out of date because the air permit application was filed in April 2026.
- The permit application, dated April 22, 2026, is at https://okdeqonbaseexternal.databankcloud.com/pav/api/Document/ATdpa%C3%81tiBf6AUlxodMaTf4RyyKtRvO65cbkkb3aVZbN4JAjNn88hU2pksW3d3Ngw9ZE27%C3%81UOLoThr916JdkRs9c%3D/?ViewerMode=PDF&ForceDownload=true. Page 11 of the PDF is the cover letter. Page 31 of the PDF, Section 2.1.1, Table 2-1, lists emission units "2G1" as "CCCT No. 3 (CTG + HRSG)" and "3G1" as "CCCT No 4 (CTG + HRSG)". These ids match EIA's generator ids for the gas turbines.

records.question: What capacity should each new Comanche block carry?
records.finding: GEM and the EIA-860M table for September 2026 at https://www.eia.gov/electricity/data/eia860m/xls/september_generator2026.xlsx show 686.4 MW per block. The Southwest Power Pool queue at https://opsportal.spp.org/Studies/GIActive shows 775.2 MW for each of the two queue entries ERAS-2025-024 and ERAS-2025-026. The air permit application at https://okdeqonbaseexternal.databankcloud.com/pav/api/Document/ATdpa%C3%81tiBf6AUlxodMaTf4RyyKtRvO65cbkkb3aVZbN4JAjNn88hU2pksW3d3Ngw9ZE27%C3%81UOLoThr916JdkRs9c%3D/?ViewerMode=PDF&ForceDownload=true says each block will produce 633 MW.
records.recommendation: Leave 686.4 MW, which is EIA's nameplate figure. Ask the project manager whether the larger queue figure should be used because it may include duct burner output.
records.researcher_notes:
This card asks what capacity new Comanche block CC2 should carry. GEM and EIA agree on 686.4 MW, but the permit application and the SPP queue show different numbers. Check the three figures below.

Where to find it:
- EIA-860M table for September 2026 at https://www.eia.gov/electricity/data/eia860m/xls/september_generator2026.xlsx. Open the sheet named "Planned". Find Plant ID 8059 and Unit Code CC2. The column "Nameplate Capacity (MW)" reads 408.8 for generator 2G1 and 277.6 for generator 2S1. Together that is 686.4 MW, the same as GEM.
- Oklahoma Department of Environmental Quality air permit application dated April 22, 2026 at https://okdeqonbaseexternal.databankcloud.com/pav/api/Document/ATdpa%C3%81tiBf6AUlxodMaTf4RyyKtRvO65cbkkb3aVZbN4JAjNn88hU2pksW3d3Ngw9ZE27%C3%81UOLoThr916JdkRs9c%3D/?ViewerMode=PDF&ForceDownload=true. Page 23 of the PDF, Section 1.1 Project Description, says "The total output of each system will be 633 MW". Page 32 of the PDF, Section 2.1.2, says the output of each combined cycle system will be "a nominal net 633 MW during summer conditions" with the duct burners on.
- SPP generator interconnection active request listing at https://opsportal.spp.org/Studies/GIActive. Two combined cycle rows are for the two new blocks, ERAS-2025-024 and ERAS-2025-026. Each row shows "Nameplate Capacity" 775.2 and "Capacity (MW)" 744. The queue does not say which entry is CC2 and which is CC3.

Why the numbers differ:
- The queue figure may be the interconnection request and not the nameplate. It may include duct burner output.
- The permit figure is a total output at one set of site conditions, not a nameplate rating. The footnote on page 23 says it reflects "Case 34" of the Mitsubishi performance data.

Not found:
- I did not find a document that gives the nameplate in plain terms.
- I searched the full text of the permit application. It does not contain 686.4, 408.8, 277.6 or the word nameplate, and it does not mention the SPP queue numbers.

records.question: Is SPP queue entry GEN-2024-321 the Cross Timbers plant?
records.finding: The Southwest Power Pool queue at https://opsportal.spp.org/Studies/GIActive lists GEN-2024-321 as a 507 MW gas project in Seminole County, connecting at the Seminole 345 kV substation, with an OG&E owner label and a 2029 in service date. The Cross Timbers permit memorandum at https://applications.deq.ok.gov/permitspublic/storedpermits/9156.pdf describes two turbines of up to 255 MW each at Section 36, Township 6N, Range 5E near Konawa. Two times 255 MW is 510 MW, close to 507 MW.
records.recommendation: Do not add a new unit for GEN-2024-321 now. Leave the queue entry linked to the Seminole station, and ask the project manager to check the queue study documents to see whether OG&E is buying Cross Timbers output.
records.researcher_notes:
Probably not the same project. The queue entry GEN-2024-321 connects at the Seminole plant and names OG&E, and nothing I found ties Cross Timbers Power LLC to it. The project manager should check the queue study documents.

Where to find it:
- Southwest Power Pool queue list at https://opsportal.spp.org/Studies/GIActive. The same list downloads as a table at https://opsportal.spp.org/Studies/GenerateActiveCSV. Find the row with Generation Interconnection Number GEN-2024-321.
- That row reads Nearest Town or County Seminole, State OK, TO at POI OGE, Substation or Line Seminole 345 kV Substation, Fuel Type Gas, Nameplate Capacity 507, In-Service Date 3/22/2029, Commercial Operation Date 4/30/2030, Status DISIS STAGE. Its Capacity column reads 493.
- Cross Timbers: Oklahoma Department of Environmental Quality permit memorandum dated October 31, 2025, at https://applications.deq.ok.gov/permitspublic/storedpermits/9156.pdf. Page 1 of the PDF gives Section 36, Township 6N, Range 5E, Seminole County. Page 2 of the PDF, in the equipment tables, lists two Siemens SGT6-5000F turbines at 255-MW each. Two times 255 MW is 510 MW, close to 507 MW.

Why I think it is different:
- Nothing I found ties Cross Timbers Power LLC to the queue entry. The queue names OG&E and a substation at the Seminole plant. The point of interconnection is the main reason I think it is a different project.

Not found:
- A web search found no news about Cross Timbers Power.
- I did not open the queue study documents for GEN-2024-321.

records.question: Should units 11 and 12 stay operating when EIA still shows testing?
records.finding: OG&E said in September 2026 that unit 11 passed its tests and would enter service in October. The October 28, 2026 earnings call at https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/transcript-oge-energy-q3-earnings-call-highlights-2026-10-28/ describes both units as added capacity. The EIA-860M table for September 2026 at https://www.eia.gov/electricity/data/eia860m/xls/september_generator2026.xlsx still shows both as construction complete, not yet in commercial operation, planned October 2026.
records.recommendation: Leave both units as operating. Check the OG&E ribbon cutting release in November 2026 for the exact date.
records.researcher_notes:
Keep units 11 and 12 as operating. The federal table is a month or more behind the company statements.

Where to find it:
- The OGE Energy third quarter earnings call summary on MarketBeat (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/transcript-oge-energy-q3-earnings-call-highlights-2026-10-28/): the Key Points and the section "Generation Expansion Centers on Horseshoe Lake" say units 11 and 12 "added approximately 448 MW".
- An OG&E news release (https://www.oge.com/web/portal/-/208-og-e-completes-horseshoe-lake-unit-11-ahead-of-schedule-and-under-budget) is titled "OG&E completes Horseshoe Lake Unit 11 ahead of schedule and under budget" and is dated September 10, 2026. It says unit 11 "passed all contractual performance tests on Aug. 31 and is expected to enter commercial service next month". It also says "Unit 12 is also expected to enter commercial operation in October."
- The EIA-860M table for September 2026 (https://www.eia.gov/electricity/data/eia860m/xls/september_generator2026.xlsx), Planned sheet, plant 2951 Horseshoe Lake, generators 11 and 12: 224 MW each, planned operation October 2026, status "(TS) Construction complete, but not yet in commercial operation".

Why this differs:
- The call summary and the release are newer than the September 2026 federal table, which has not yet moved the units to the Operating sheet.

Not found:
- No document gives the exact commercial operation date for either unit. I looked at the release, the call summary and the federal table.

Next check:
- The OG&E ribbon cutting release expected in November 2026 should give the date.
